events.title: March on Washington and 'I Have a Dream' Speech
events.description: Approximately 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., for the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech, calling for an end to racism and for civil and economic rights for all Americans.
events.significance: The march and speech became defining moments of the American civil rights movement and helped build momentum for the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: First Issue of Scientific American Published
events.description: Rufus Porter launched Scientific American as a weekly broadsheet newspaper focused on inventions, patents, and technological progress.
events.significance: It became the oldest continuously published magazine in the United States and a leading venue for communicating science to the general public.

events.title: Birth of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
events.description: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was born in Frankfurt, in the Holy Roman Empire. He became a poet, playwright, novelist, and scientist, best known for works such as Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther.
events.significance: Goethe is regarded as one of the greatest figures in German and world literature and a major influence on Romanticism and European intellectual life.

events.title: Iraq Declares Kuwait Its 19th Province
events.description: Weeks after invading Kuwait in August 1990, Iraq's government under Saddam Hussein formally announced the annexation of Kuwait as Iraq's 19th province.
events.significance: The annexation was condemned internationally and led to UN sanctions and ultimately the U.S.-led coalition's military action in the 1991 Gulf War.

events.title: Hurricane Katrina Prompts Mandatory Evacuation of New Orleans
events.description: As Hurricane Katrina intensified into a Category 5 storm in the Gulf of Mexico, New Orleans Mayor Ray Nagin ordered the first-ever mandatory evacuation of the city.
events.significance: Katrina made landfall the next day, causing catastrophic flooding and more than 1,800 deaths, and exposed serious failures in disaster preparedness and response in the United States.
